## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over identity-ordered AoS with fused mask+list intermediates can approach the streaming ceiling at low death rates, where the branchy respawn path is rarely taken.

## Layout & approach
The 73 B/particle AoS offers 11 fields, but fused loops touch only fractions: loop 1 uses 28 of 68 B (41% hot), loop 2 uses 4 of 68 B (5% hot), loop 3 uses 28 of 68 B (41% hot). The remaining 59–95% is dead weight per cache line. No intermediate storage — the death verdict stays in registers — so fusion avoids a second pass but cannot avoid re-reading the 68-byte stride. With 128-byte lines holding ~1.9 particles, roughly half each fill is wasted.

## Cache saturation
The ns/particle curve is flat across all N at every death rate — not cache-bound. At q=0.01, cost holds at 8.0–8.4 ns/p from L1d (N=380) through DRAM (N=10M), with no knee at the L1d spill (N≈897) or L2 spill (N≈57456). L1d→L2 adds ~0.1 ns/p; L2→DRAM slightly improves cost (8.3→8.0), as sequential stride-68B prefetch is as effective from DRAM as from cache. The dense grid resolves both but neither is performance-relevant.

## Bandwidth
The memory floor is 2.441 ns/p; at q=0.01 the algo runs at 8.0–8.4 ns/p (3.3x above floor), achieving 8.5–9.1 GB/s — 29–30% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling. With 41% hot bytes, useful bandwidth is ~3.7 GB/s. Compute-bound at q=0.01 (compute=64–71%, branch_flush=5–8%), transitioning to branch-bound by q=0.25 (branch_flush=36%) and q=0.5 (42%). BW collapses from 9.1 to 4.0 GB/s as q rises. Vs baseline: 1.1x at q=0.01, 1.35x at q=0.5. Vs winner: 1.7–3.4x slower, widening with q.

## Assembly
Partial vectorization: `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` on 4-lane position vectors, `ext.16b` for lane shuffling. But `ld1.s {v17}[1]` is a single-element gather breaking the stream. Death is per-particle via `fcmp` + `b.lt`/`b.ge` — branchy, not blended — written with `strb` (byte-granular scatter). Loop 2 carries 9 cond-branches and ~85 insns/iter, dominated by PRNG refill (`bl _Random.init__anon_28827.gen.fill`). Render and spawn are delegated via `bl`. Only 18/240 insns are vector-suffixed. The `strb` scatter and branchy death cap bandwidth at 30% of ceiling despite sequential stride.

## Verdict
Refuted — never approaches the streaming ceiling (30% at best) and always 1.7–3.4x slower than the winner. At q=0.01: 1.1x faster than naive but 2.1x slower than the winner (8.0 vs ~4.2 ns/p) — the 41% hot fraction and `strb` scatter cap useful bandwidth at ~3.7 GB/s. At q=0.5: 1.35x faster than naive but 3.4x slower than the winner (18.2 vs ~5.4 ns/p), as branch_flush rises to 42% and the 9-branch respawn path dominates. The mask+list intermediate cannot overcome AoS dead-weight or the branchy per-particle death decision.
